Variance-component (VC / SKAT-style) multi-trait test

Source: vignettes/method-vc.Rmd
method-vc.Rmd

Function: run_vc()

Result column: vc

Family: Multiple-association omnibus

Introduction

MPAT/MTAR multi-phenotype association test of the SKAT variance-component family. It scores the squared length of the whitened-then-whitened-again Z-vector Σ−1z\Sigma^{-1} z; under the null this is a weighted sum of chi-squares whose weights are the eigenvalues of Σ−1\Sigma^{-1}, and its tail is evaluated numerically.

Mathematical Framework and Implementation

For a variant with per-trait Z-score vector z=(z1,…,zK)′z = (z_1,\dots,z_K)', zk=β̂k/se(β̂k)z_k = \hat\beta_k / \mathrm{se}(\hat\beta_k), over KK phenotypes, let s=Σ−1zs = \Sigma^{-1} z, where Σ\Sigma is the K×KK \times K trait correlation matrix and Σ−1\Sigma^{-1} (Sinv) is precomputed once. The variance-component statistic is

T=s′s=(Σ−1z)′(Σ−1z)=z′Σ−2z. T = s' s = (\Sigma^{-1} z)'(\Sigma^{-1} z) = z'\, \Sigma^{-2}\, z.

This is the SKAT-type score for a random-effects (variance-component) model in which the per-trait effects are treated as exchangeable random effects with kernel Σ−2\Sigma^{-2}.

Under the global null z∼𝒩(0,Σ)z \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \Sigma) one has s=Σ−1z∼𝒩(0,Σ−1)s = \Sigma^{-1} z \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \Sigma^{-1}), so with eigenvalues μ1≥…≥μK>0\mu_1 \ge \dots \ge \mu_K > 0 of Σ−1\Sigma^{-1} (equivalently μk=1/λk\mu_k = 1/\lambda_k for eigenvalues λk\lambda_k of Σ\Sigma; stored as eval_Sinv)

T=d∑k=1Kμkχ1,k2. T \;\stackrel{d}{=}\; \sum_{k=1}^{K} \mu_k\, \chi^2_{1,k}.

The p-value

p=Pr⁡(∑kμkχ1,k2≥T) p = \Pr\!\Big(\sum_{k} \mu_k \chi^2_{1,k} \ge T\Big)

is computed by the Davies-labeled numerical inversion, with the modified Liu moment-matching approximation as a fallback when Davies returns a value outside (0,1)(0,1).

What This Method Advances

VC uses a SKAT-style variance-component perspective over phenotypes, emphasizing squared evidence across correlation-adjusted trait directions.

Assumptions

Because the weights are the eigenvalues of Σ−1\Sigma^{-1}, VC up-weights the low-variance directions of Σ\Sigma (the directions in which the traits are nearly independent or anti-correlated), the opposite emphasis to the WI test (run_wi()). It is a dense, omnibus variance-component test, most powerful when effects spread across the trait-decorrelated directions, and it can be sensitive when Σ\Sigma is near-singular (small λk\lambda_k inflate μk\mu_k). Validity requires a correctly specified, non-singular Σ\Sigma and approximately Gaussian null Z-scores.

When This Method Is a Good Fit

Good for omnibus variance-component signal across correlation-adjusted trait directions.

The implementation treats variants independently and relies on the trait-correlation estimate derived from the available summary statistics unless an individual method estimates a pairwise null moment internally.

Minimal Usage 

library(pleioverse)
set.seed(1)
pleio <- run_pleiosim(
  n_phenotype = 3, n_participant = 500,
  n_variant_pleiotropic = 3,
  n_variant_nonpleiotropic = c(3, 3, 3),
  n_variant_null = 30,
  heritability = c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3)
)
pleio <- run_vc(pleio)
head(pleio@results$vc)

Implementation Files

  • R wrapper: R/run_vc.R
  • C++ kernel or dispatcher: src/vc.cpp
  • Shared MPAT inputs, where applicable: R/pleiotest.R and src/test_engine.cpp
